subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain one-shot-only and be rejected for recurring schedules?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode conflicting lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects existing persisted jobs, future defaults, and session-state retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add an upgrade/load/doctor path for omitted persisted isolated jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only rejection
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its caller and upgrade gaps are addressed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land only the new create default and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add an upgrade/load/doctor path for omitted persisted isolated jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron defaulting, SQLite persistence, and compatibility semantics where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
